transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-18
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood Solutions), Marco (CTO - LatticeWorks), Leah (Head of Search), Samir (Eng Lead), Nina (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, rough): Quick hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + reranking for LatticeWorks product search. Discussed sample pipeline, cost/latency tradeoffs, VPC vs hosted, SOC 2 and KMS for PII, and next steps for a 2-week POC.

Topics: 
- Hosted embeddings endpoint and reranker endpoint
- Console and Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization)
- Security (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs)
- Benchmark plan and data handoff

[00:00:08] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account. Quick introductions?
[00:00:14] Marco: Marco here, CTO at LatticeWorks. We've got Leah, Samir, and Nina with me. Thanks for doing this.
[00:00:20] Leah: Hi all, Leah — we're primarily focused on improving our search relevance on product pages, reduce the false positives, and especially rerank for long-tail queries.
[00:00:27] Alex: Great, that's perfect. Priya, do you want to drive?
[00:00:30] Priya: Sure — hi everyone. I'll walk through the hosted API flow: embeddings for retrieval, then a lightweight reranker for top-K. We'll do demo calls from the console and show a small sample of Optimize suggestions.
[00:00:42] Samir: Quick note — we're currently using an embedding store in Postgres with FAISS on top, and a small transformer for reranking hosted on our cluster. Latency target is <150ms p95 for product pages, cost is also a big factor.
[00:00:55] Priya: Got it. That's a common balance we see. For hosted API we can usually hit sub-100ms token latency for the reranker with our lower-latency variants, but cost per request depends a lot on sequence length and batch size. We'll show how Optimize can recommend batching and quantization to bring down unit cost.
[00:01:13] Marco: When you say "hosted" — this is Redwood's cloud, right? What about data residency and audit logs?
[00:01:20] Alex: Yes hosted is our cloud control plane; we keep customer data isolated per tenancy. For audit logs and retention, we have options; also Redwood Private (VPC) is available if you require customer-managed networking. Nina, curious if you need SOC 2 artifacts?
[00:01:34] Nina: We do, and also KMS integration and proof of at-rest encryption. Also we need to understand how long embeddings or caching are retained in the hosted offering.
[00:01:42] Priya: Absolutely — we retain KV cache for a short TTL by default and don't persist raw request payloads for longer than retention. But we can also turn off prefix caching for sensitive workflows. We'll share the security pack with SOC 2, KMS/HSM integration notes and sample audit logs.
[00:01:56]
[00:02:04] -- Priya shares the Console — link dropped to the deck and a sandbox: https://redwood.example/sandbox/lattice-run
[00:02:12] Priya: Ok jumping into the console. First the embeddings endpoint: you POST a batch of text, get back 768/1536-d vectors depending on model, then store in your vector DB. We have precomputed benchmarks — you can choose a smaller-embedding model to trade quality for cost.
[00:02:28] Leah: Can you show how the rerank call looks? We want to keep the retrieval step cheap and only run the reranker on top-k of 50 or less.
[00:02:36] Priya: Yep. We'll do: retrieve top-200 via vector search in your store, then call Redwood reranker endpoint with those candidates and the query as context. The reranker returns scores and a tie-breaker explanation field if you ask for structured output.
[00:02:49] Samir: Explanation field — is that deterministic? We need to be careful about hallucinated reasons.
[00:02:55] Priya: Good call — the explanation is a model-derived rationale; it's best used as a signal not as a log of truth. You can also request structured labels (e.g., category match, exact SKU match) if you pass some product metadata.
[00:03:07] Alex: Also Optimize can suggest feature flags — for example, if you have frequent long-tail queries we might recommend heavier reranker models on canary paths and fallback to cheaper variants.
[00:03:16] Marco: Pricing — do you have per-token + per-embedding charges? How does reranker pricing work?
[00:03:22] Alex: Yes hosted pricing is per-embedding vector and per-token for reranker use. For reranker we typically show per-request unit based on avg tokens processed; we'll send an estimate for your 5M monthly queries scenario.
[00:03:33]
[00:03:40] [00:03:40] Priya: Demo time — I'll run a sample query. (sound of keyboard) This is a bit rough in the live console transcription, bear with me.
[00:03:50] [00:03:50] Priya: POST /v1/embeddings with 500 product titles — response 200 in 320ms, vector dims 1536. Then we index to their FAISS example.
[00:04:03] [00:04:03] Priya: Now simulate a user query "waterproof hiking jacket for heavy rain" — retrieve top-100, rerank top-12 with our mid-tier reranker model.
[00:04:15] [00:04:15] Priya: Reranker return: p95 latency ~112ms on this hosted region, scores normalized. You can see the top result moved up because of SKU exact-match boost and weather-rating metadata.
[00:04:30] Leah: Nice — can we surface business rules, like "always prefer in-stock items"?
[00:04:36] Priya: Yes, pass that as a hard constraint in the rerank request — we'll filter candidates before scoring or apply a large negative bias if out-of-stock.
[00:04:44] Samir: How do you pass metadata? We store attributes in Postgres.
[00:04:49] Priya: The reranker accepts an array of candidates with optional metadata fields; the model isn't the only signal — you can give feature flags and we can add learned features into the scoring function.
[00:04:59]
[00:05:10] [00:05:10] Marco: About caching: we need to avoid storing PII-derived embeddings persistently. Can blade disable caching? (misheard 'blade' for 'please')
[00:05:18] Priya: Yes, you can disable prefix/KV caching per-route. Also you can set TTL to 0 so nothing persists. We'll call that out in the security doc.
[00:05:26] Nina: And KMS — do you support customer-managed keys?
[00:05:29] Alex: Yes KMS/HSM integrations for Private and dedicated options, and hosted can integrate with CMKs for certain enterprise plans. We'll include the KMS architecture diagram.
[00:05:40]
[00:05:48] [00:05:48] Priya: Switching briefly to Optimize — here's a suggestion panel. It looks at your latency/cost and suggests quantize-int8 for the reranker at lower sequence lengths, and also suggests batching windows for your traffic patterns. It also recommended a 50ms latency SLO headroom for the hosted variant.
[00:06:05] Leah: Do you have historical trace-based suggestions? We can upload a trace of 10k requests?
[00:06:11] Priya: Yes, the Console accepts trace exports; Optimize will run a simulated pass and recommend batch sizes and model flavors. That demo we ran was from a synthetic set — we'll run it on your traces during the POC.
[00:06:24] Samir: If we do batching, do we risk tail latency spikes?
[00:06:29] Priya: There's a tradeoff — continuous batching helps throughput but increases p99 unless you set a max latency cutoff. Optimize will show the cost/latency curve so you can pick the sweet spot.
[00:06:39]
[00:07:02] [00:07:02] Marco: For the POC, we'd like a realistic benchmark with our 10k labeled queries and expected traffic distribution. Who runs that?
[00:07:09] Alex: We can run it together — Priya will spin up the hosted test key, you hand over a sample dataset (Samir), and we'll run the benchmark in our sandbox with your retention and KMS toggles. We'll include a spreadsheet with per-unit cost and latency projections.
[00:07:24] Leah: One more question — how deterministic are reranker results across model versions? If we pin a model and then switch, how to detect regressions?
[00:07:33] Priya: Great question. Console includes evaluation dashboards and you can pin model versions per-route. We also support canary rollouts and A/B tests; Optimize raises regression alerts tied to a canonical prompt set.
[00:07:46] Samir: That will help with our QA process. We need an automated smoke test on each deploy.
[00:07:51] Priya: Exactly — you can plug in your post-deploy evals and get alerts.
[00:07:58]
[00:08:12] [00:08:12] Marco: What about fallback behavior if the hosted region is saturated? We need graceful degradation to avoid broken pages.
[00:08:20] Alex: We have smart routing and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants or to a cached ML-free ranking if the reranker times out. We can set strict SLOs and fallback policies per-route.
[00:08:32] Leah: Would fallback be visible to the user? We need telemetry to mark when fallback happened.
[00:08:37] Priya: Yes, tracing includes a flag in the request logs and Console's per-route dashboard surfaces fallback rates.
[00:08:46]
[00:09:00] [00:09:00] -- Slight crosstalk while Alex drops the pricing sheet link: https://redwood.example/pricing/lattice-5m-estimate.xlsx
[00:09:08] Alex: I'll be transparent — the hosted route is typically cheaper to get started, but at scale and strict compliance you may prefer Dedicated or Private. We'll show cost comparisons in the POC sheet.
[00:09:20] Marco: If we wanted Dedicated, how quickly can that be provisioned?
[00:09:25] Alex: Dedicated pools usually require a lead time of 4-6 weeks depending on capacity and commit. Private VPC has an extra integration window. We'll scope that if the POC hits the metrics.
[00:09:37] Nina: For contracts we need SLAs and audit support.
[00:09:40] Alex: Yep enterprise contract and compliance package is available; we'll loop in our legal and security teams in the next thread.
[00:09:48]
[00:10:05] [00:10:05] Priya: Back to the demo — quick example of a rerank request payload. (reads) "{ query: 'hiking jacket heavy rain', candidates: [ {id: 'sku123', metadata: {in_stock: true, rating: 4.2}} ... ] }". Note the metadata fields.
[00:10:23] Samir: OK — small thing — do you support chunked candidate scoring? Our products have long descriptions and we only want to pass summaries.
[00:10:29] Priya: Yes, you can pass snippets/summaries to reduce token cost. The Console also lets you pre-process and cache short embeddings of long docs to keep reranker inputs small.
[00:10:40]
[00:11:05] [00:11:05] Leah: Let's talk about evaluation metrics — we want to measure MRR, NDCG, and business metrics like conversion lift. How do you recommend instrumenting that?
[00:11:14] Priya: Start with NDCG and MRR against a labeled holdout. Then run live A/B measuring conversions. Console ties routing and model-level metrics to revenue signals if you pass conversion events.
[00:11:27] Marco: If we do A/B, can you automate rollouts when conversion improves?
[00:11:31] Alex: We support automated rollouts with a threshold gate — if the canary exceeds conversion by X% we can widen rollout. It's configurable by route.
[00:11:40]
[00:12:02] [00:12:02] -- Priya runs a short transformer explanation example; some words are garbled in transcript here: "...re-ranker does a top pull, uh, top, top shift..."
[00:12:12] Priya: Apologies for the noisy demo — live consoles sometimes misreport latency when my local network spikes. But results are saved in the notebook and we'll send a recording.
[00:12:25] Alex: To close the loop, Samir, can you share 10k labeled queries and a small production-like trace? That will let us run the realistic benchmark.
[00:12:34] Samir: Yes, we can. We'll anonymize PII and export traces by tomorrow.
[00:12:39] Nina: We'll review security pack first. If any gaps, we might require Private.
[00:12:44] Alex: Understood — we'll push the security pack immediately after this call.
[00:12:50]
[00:12:58] [00:12:58] -- Quick digression: competitor question from Marco: "Why not just use OpenAI endpoints?"
[00:13:04] Marco: Right, we evaluated OpenAI and others — main asks are latency, cost predictability, and enterprise controls.
[00:13:10] Alex: Good question. Redwood focuses on inference economics and offering multiple deployment modes plus fine-grained SLOs and tooling for rollouts and canaries. We'll share benchmark comparisons but main value is the hosting + console + Optimize feedback loop.
[00:13:24]
[00:13:40] [00:13:40] Priya: Ok last part — quick walkthrough of rerank tuning. We have a prompt-template and a small supervised loss option if you want to train a lightweight linear combiner on top of model scores. That often reduces cost and is more deterministic.
[00:13:56] Leah: So you mean we can keep the heavy model only for hard queries and use a linear model for the rest?
[00:14:01] Priya: Exactly. Optimize will help pick the boundary based on traffic distribution.
[00:14:08] Samir: Any throttles on the hosted tier? Will we be rate-limited?
[00:14:14] Alex: Basic rate limits apply but they're configurable in enterprise plans; for the POC we'll provision a higher quota.
[00:14:21]
[00:14:40] [00:14:40] -- 10 minute mark summary by Alex: POC plan: Lattice provides 10k labeled queries + traces; Redwood runs hosted test in sandbox, returns spreadsheet with latency/cost, shares security pack. If POC meets p95 <150ms and cost targets, discuss Dedicated/Private procurement.
[00:14:58] Marco: That sounds right.
[00:15:04] Leah: One more security nuance — data residency for EU users; we have EU subset customers.
[00:15:10] Alex: We have region routing and can route EU traffic to EU hosted region; for data residency contracts we'll document where embeddings live.
[00:15:19] Nina: Also need RBAC and SSO (SAML).
[00:15:22] Priya: Both supported; Console supports SAML SSO and role-based access controls, audit logs exportable.
[00:15:33]
[00:15:50] [00:15:50] -- Priya flips to a short Optimize chart showing cost/latency curves (link to live mock).
[00:15:58] Priya: Example: with quantized reranker and batching we can drop token-cost by ~40% with a 10-15ms median latency change; p99 needs careful tuning.
[00:16:11]
[00:16:30] [00:16:30] Marco: Ok let's talk timeline. We want POC results in two weeks. Is that feasible?
[00:16:35] Alex: Yes — if we get data by tomorrow and Redwood runs overnight tests, you should have an initial report within 10 business days.
[00:16:43] Samir: We'll prioritize the dataset.
